<!-- pr-reviewer: c5bf96ec21f38225b6ee62843cad98562d75f550 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is an independent review. The change touches STEP import geometry, so it is a safety-tier review.

## What looks good

- Edge curves and swept generators now share the metered budget design of issue 1536. Each edge gets its own meter per pass. A swept generator uses its face's meter.
- A refused division returns a two-point stub, never a partial grid. The pass is refused by name before any mesh can pass. The edge refusal names the edge position, the edge count and the shell id. The face refusal keeps naming the face and its kind.
- The refusal sets `continuous: false`. A coarser pass can therefore not hide a jumped edge (#1568 fallback law respected).
- The knot jump check is safe arithmetic: `checked_sub`, `saturating_add`, and bound checks before each index. A zero-weight rational curve dehomogenises to non-finite points, and the probe check rejects it before the budget can burn.
- A refused revolution collapses its generator onto the axis. truck then cannot build an angular grid from a false radius. The pin `a_refused_revolution_does_not_divide_a_bogus_radius` checks this.
- The division stops on a stale midpoint (`m == a || m == b`) and at depth 100. Each probe spends one meter unit. The work is bounded with no wall-clock thread left behind.
- The pins are good: 3 integration refusal tests with a 20 second barrier, plus 10 new unit tests. The exact-compare tests hold truck's output for healthy curves, with transforms and reversal.

## Results, merged with main

The head merged cleanly into origin/main (`7c514c874`). No conflict. No source of the change was edited. All results ran locally in the review worktree.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1 step, ok in 46 s. It ran the app lib tests and the 18 mapped import suites.
- Passed: 389. Failed: 0. Ignored: 2 (both existing heavy-lane tests).
- The new suite `import_step_curve_guard` passed: 3 of 3, in 0.01 s. The refusals trip the budget; nothing hangs.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git diff --stat` against main shows the 7 files of the PR. No golden, no `.nc` or `.cl` output change. No snapshot PNG change.

## Law checks

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the production code of the diff. The new `expect` and `panic` calls are inside tests.
- Provenance line: present. It cites truck's published `parameter_division` (Apache-2.0) and the NURBS Book. No vendor material.
- No new crate dependency. No process file change, so no `Process change:` line is needed.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and a closing reference to issue 1545. The commit subject is conventional.
- The new test file sits in `crates/app/tests/` and imports `camcraft_app` items. Its Gate map names `app::geometry::import`. Placement is correct.
- No UI change, so no structural test or command law applies.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes (not blocking)

1. `step_guard.rs` is now 403 lines and `step_guard_tests.rs` is 414 lines. They are past the 400-line guidance. A later task can split them along the face / edge seam.
2. `CurveGuard::subs`, `der` and `der2` pass through to truck without a charge. Only the bounded division probes are metered. Nothing in the tessellation path recurses through these calls, so the pass stays bounded. A future metered search would need the charge.
3. The byte-identical claim rests on the exact-compare pins and the passing golden suites. The full external STEP corpus and the release heavy lane were not run here. The cut will cover them.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
